questions.q: A nucleus $A,$ with a finite de-broglie wavelength ${\lambda}_{A},$ undergoes spontaneous fission into two nuclei $B$ and $C$ of equal mass. $B$ flies in the same direction as that of $A,$ while $C$ flies in the opposite direction with a velocity equal to half of that of $B .$ The de-Broglie wavelengths ${\lambda}_{B}$ and ${\lambda}_{C}$ of B and C are respectively:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{h}{\lambdaA} = \dfrac{h}{\lambdaB} - \dfrac{h}{\lambdaC}$ …(i)
Also ${\lambda}_{C} = 2{\lambda}_{B}$ ...(ii)
From equation (i) & (ii),
$\dfrac{1}{{\lambda}_{A}} = \dfrac{1}{{\lambda}_{B}} - \dfrac{1}{2{\lambda}_{B}}$
${\lambda}_{B} = \dfrac{{\lambda}_{A}}{2}; {\lambda}_{C} = {\lambda}_{A}$

questions.q:
In photoelectric effect an em-wave is incident on a metal surface and electrons are ejected from the surface. If the work function of the metal is 2.14 eV and stopping potential is 2 V , what is the wavelength of the em-wave ?
(Given hc $=1242 \mathrm{eVnm}$ where h is the Planck's constant and c is the speed of light in vaccum.)
questions.subject: Physics

questions.q:
The threshold wavelength for photoelectric emission from a material is $5500\overset{∘}{A}$. Photoelectrons will be emitted, when this material is illuminated with monochromatic radiation from a

A.~$75W$ infra-red lamp

B.~$10W$ infra-red lamp

C.~$75W$ ultra-violet lamp

D.~$10W$ ultra-violet lamp

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here, threshold wavelength& ${λ}_{th} = 5500Å = 550nm$

For photoelectric emission,~the wavelength of the light should be less than~$550$ nm.

Wavelength of infrared radiation~extends from $700nm - 1mm$~and that of ultraviolet radiation is~$100 - 400nm$.

Since, UV light has less wavelength than~$550$ nm, so only UV would be able to emit photoelectrons.

For the photoelectric effect, the maximum kinetic energy \left({E}_{k}\right)$ of the photoelectrons is plotted against the frequency $( v )$ of the incident photons as shown in figure. The slope of the graph gives

questions.q: The de Broglie wavelengths for an electron and a photon are ${λ}_{e}$~and ${λ}_{p}$ respectively. For the same kinetic energy of electron and photon, which of the following presents the correct relation between the de Broglie wavelengths of two?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
De-Broglie wavelength for electron is given by,& ${λ}_{e} = \dfrac{h}{2mk}$

For photon $k = \dfrac{hc}{\lambdap} ⇒ {λ}_{p} = \dfrac{hc}{k}$. Therefore,

${λ}_{e} = \dfrac{h\sqrt{{λ}_{p}}}{2mhc}$

${λ}_{p} ∝ {\lambdae}^{2}$

questions.q: In a photoelectric experiment, increasing the intensity of incident light:
options: increases the number of photons incident and also increases the K.E. of the ejected electrons.
increases the frequency of photons incident and increases the K.E. of the ejected electrons.
increases the number of photons incident and the K.E. of the ejected electrons remains unchanged.
increases the frequency of photons incident and the K.E. of the ejected electrons remains unchanged.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: The relation between the energy of photons and the intensity of photons is,& $hv = \dfrac{IA}{n}$, where~$n$& is the number of photons, if we increase the number of photons then frequency does not change it means total energy and kinetic energy of photon remains unchanged but due to to this property the intensity of light is increased.

questions.q: When photon of energy $4.0$ eV strikes the surface of a metal $A,$ the ejected photoelectrons have maximum kinetic energy ${T}_{A}eV$ and de-Broglie wavelength ${\lambda}_{A} .$ The maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons liberated from another metal $B$ by photon of energy $4.50$ eV is ${T}_{B} = \left({T}_{A} - 1.5\right)eV .$ If the de-Broglie wavelength of these photoelectrons ${\lambda}_{B} = 2{\lambda}_{A},$ then the work function of metal $B$ is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Relation between de-Broglie wavelength and K.E. is
$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2 ( KE ) {m}_{e}}} ⇒ \lambda ∝ \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{KE}}$
$\dfrac{{\lambda}_{A}}{{\lambda}_{B}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{K{E}_{B}}}{\sqrt{K{E}_{A}}}$
$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{{T}_{A} - 1.5}{TA}} ⇒ {T}_{A} = 2eV$
$∴ K{E}_{B} = 2 - 1.5 = 0.5eV$
${ϕ}_{B} = 4.5 - 0.5 = 4eV$

questions.q: A parallel beam of light of wavelength $900$ nm and intensity $100{Wm}^{- 2}$ is incident on a surface perpendicular to the beam. The~number of photons crossing $1{cm}^{2}$ area perpendicular to the beam in one second is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Wavelength of incident beam $\lambda = 900 \times {10}^{- 9}m$

Energy of a single photon~$E = \dfrac{hc}{λ}$.

Intensity is defined as power per unit area. Therefore,

Intensity of incident beam $I = \dfrac{E}{tA}$

If the number of photons crossing the given area per second is~$n$, then

$n = \dfrac{Enet}{Esinglepholon} = \dfrac{IA\lambda}{hc}$

$⇒ n = \dfrac{\left(100\right)\left(1 \times {10}^{- 4}\right)\left(900 \times {10}^{- 9}\right)}{6 . 62 \times {10}^{- 34} \times 3 \times {10}^{8}} = 4 . 5 \times {10}^{16}$.

questions.q: If the deBroglie wavelength of an electron is equal to $10^{-}$ times the wavelength of a photon of frequency $6 \times 10^{14}\mathrm{Hz}$, then the speed of electron is equal to : (Speed of light  \left.=3 \times 10^{8} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\right)$ Planck's constant $=6.63 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{~J} . \mathrm{s}$ Mass of electron  \left.=9.1 \times 10^{-31} \mathrm{~kg}\right)$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$de-Broglie wavelength, \lambda=$\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{mv}}=10^{-3}\left(\frac{3 \times 10^{8}}{6 \times 10^{14}}\right) \quad \left[\because \lambda=\frac{\mathrm{c}}{\mathrm{v}}\right]$
$v=\frac{6.63 \times 10^{-34} \times 6 \times 10^{14}}{9.1 \times 10^{-31} \times 3 \times 10^{5}}$
v=1.45 \times10^{6} m / s
$

questions.q: Average force exerted on a non-reflecting surface at normal incidence is $2.4 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~N}$. If $360 \mathrm{~W} / \mathrm{cm}^2$ is the light energy flux during span of 1 hour 30 minutes, Then the area of the surface is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Pressure }=\frac{I}{C}=\frac{F}{A} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{360}{10^{-4} \times 3 \times 10^8}=\frac{2.4 \times 10^{-4}}{A} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{A}=2 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~m}^2=0.02 \mathrm{~m}^2\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A proton and an $\alpha$-particle are accelerated from rest by $2V$ and $4V$ potentials, respectively. The ratio of their de-Broglie wavelength is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the de Broglie wavelength of the proton is given by

${λ}_{p} = \dfrac{h}{2{m}_{p}{q}_{p}V} . . . \left(1\right)$

The formula to calculate the de Broglie wavelength of the alpha particle is given by

${λ}_{α} = $\dfrac{h}{2{m}_{α}{q}_{α}V '} . . . \left(2\right)$

Divide equation (1) by equation (2) and simplify to obtain the required ratio.

\dfrac{\lambdap}{\lambda\alpha} = \dfrac{{m}_{α}}{{m}_{p}} \times \sqrt{\dfrac{{q}_{α}V '}{{q}_{p}V}} . . . \left(3\right)$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (3) to calculate the required ratio.

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{\lambdap}{\lambda\alpha}& = & \sqrt{\dfrac{4}{1}} \times \sqrt{\dfrac{2 \times 4}{1 \times 2}}\\ & = & 4: 1\end{cases}

$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement $I:$ Two photons having equal linear momenta have equal wavelengths.

Statement $II:$ If the wavelength of the photon is decreased, then the momentum and energy of a photon will also decrease.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement $I$ and Statement $II$ are false
Both Statement $I$ and Statement $II$ are true
Statement $I$ is true but Statement $II$ is false
Statement $I$ is false but Statement $II$ is true
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
If linear momentum are equal then wavelength also equal.

The momentum& $p$~and energy~$E$~of a photon is given by,

$p = \dfrac{h}{λ}, E = \dfrac{hc}{λ}$; where~$c$~is speed of light and~$h$& is Plank's constant.

On decreasing wavelength, momentum and energy of photon increases.

questions.q: Particle $A$ of mass ${m}_{A} = \dfrac{m}{2}$ moving along the $\text{x}$ -axis with velocity ${v}_{0}$ collides elastically with another particle $\text{B}$ at rest having mass ${m}_{B} = \dfrac{m}{3}$. If both the particles move along the $\text{x}$ -axis after the collision, the change $∆ \lambda$ in the wavelength of the particle $\text{A}$, in terms of its de-Broglie wavelength  \left({λ}_{0}\right)$ before the collision is:$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
${v}_{1} = 2\left(m / 3\right)0\left(\dfrac{m}{2} + \dfrac{m}{3}\right) + \left(\dfrac{m}{2} - \dfrac{m}{3}\right)v\left(\dfrac{m}{2} + \dfrac{m}{3}\right) = \dfrac{v}{5}$

For particle~$A$,

Initial de-Broglie wavelength

${λ}_{0} = \dfrac{h}{\dfrac{m}{2}v} = \dfrac{2h}{mv}$

Final de-Broglie wavelength after collision.

${λ}_{1} = \dfrac{h}{\dfrac{m}{2}\dfrac{v}{5}} = \dfrac{10h}{mv} = 5{λ}_{0}$

Change in De-Broglie wavelength~$\Delta \lambda = {λ}_{i} - {λ}_{0} = 4{λ}_{0}$

questions.q: Light is incident normally on a completely absorbing surface with an energy flux of $25Wcm^{- 2}$ . If the surface has an area of $25cm^{2}$ , the momentum transferred to the surface in $\text{40}\text\min$ time duration will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The power of the incident light is& $P = 25Wcm^{- 2} \times 25cm^{2}$
$= 625W$
Energy incident per second, $E = \dfrac{hc}{λ} = 625J$
Momentum incident per second, $p = \dfrac{E}{c} = \dfrac{h}{λ} = \dfrac{625}{c}$
$∴$ Total momentum transferred to the surface~$= \dfrac{625}{c} \times 40 \times 60$
$= 5 \times {10}^{- 3}Ns$

questions.q: An electron in the ground state of the hydrogen atom has the orbital radius of $5.3 \times 10^{-11} \mathrm{~m}$ while that for the electron in third excited state is $8.48 \times 10^{-10} \mathrm{~m}$. The ratio of the de Broglie wavelengths of electron in the excited state to that in the ground state is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\lambda=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{mv}}$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{mvr}=\frac{\mathrm{nh}}{2 \pi} \\
& \mathrm{mv}=\frac{\mathrm{nh}}{2 \pi \mathrm{r}} \\
& \lambda=\frac{2 \pi \mathrm{rh}}{\mathrm{nh}} \\
& \lambda \propto \frac{\mathrm{r}}{\mathrm{n}} \\
& \frac{\lambda_1}{\lambda_4}=\frac{\mathrm{r}_1 \mathrm{n}_4}{\mathrm{n}_1 \mathrm{r}_4}=\frac{5.3 \times 10^{-11} \times 4}{1 \times 84.8 \times 10^{-11}} \\
& \frac{\lambda_1}{\lambda_4}=\frac{1}{4}
\end{aligned}$$

questions.q: In an experiment with photoelectric effect, the stopping potential,
options: increases with increase in the intensity of the incident light
decreases with increase in the intensity of the incident light
increases with increase in the wavelength of the incident light
is  \left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{e}}\right)$ times the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From Einstein photoelectric equation
$\frac{h c}{\lambda}=\phi+e V_S$ Maximum K.E. $=(\mathrm{K})_{\max }=e V s$
So, $V_S=\frac{(\mathrm{K})_{\max }}{e}$

questions.q: The ratio of wavelengths of proton and deuteron accelerated by potential ${V}_{p}$~and ${V}_{d}$~is $1: \sqrt{2}$. Then, the ratio of ${V}_{p}$~to ${V}_{d}$& will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Kinetic energy gained by a charged particle accelerated by a potential& $V$~is~$qV$

$KE = qV$

Using relation between momentum and kinetic energy

$⇒ \dfrac{p2}{2m} = qV ⇒ p = \sqrt{2mqV}$

We know that momentum of charged particle is~$p = \dfrac{h}{λ}$.

Thus,~$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{2mqV}$

Now,~$\dfrac{\lambdap}{\lambdad} = \sqrt{\dfrac{{m}_{d}{V}_{d}}{{m}_{p}{V}_{p}}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2{V}_{d}}{Vp}} ⇒ \dfrac{Vp}{Vd} = 4$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : Stopping potential in photoelectric effect does not depend on the power of the light source.

Statement II : For a given metal, the maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectron depends on the wavelength of the incident light.

In the light of above statements, choose the most& appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Both statement I and statement II are correct
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Stopping potential depends on frequency of incident light and nature of the emitter material. It is& independent of the power of the light source.

Maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons is stated as$K{E}_\max = hν - ϕ = \dfrac{hc}{λ} - ϕ$,~Where, $h$ is the Planck’s constant,~$ν$~is the frequency,~$\lambda$~is wavelength of incident light and~$ϕ$& is the work function of the metal surface.

Thus,& the maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectron depends on the wavelength of the incident light.

So both statements I and II are correct

questions.q: An electron (of mass $m$ ) and a photon have the same energy $E$ in the range of a few $eV$. The ratio of the de-Broglie wavelength associated with the electron and the wavelength of the photon is ( $c =$ speed of light in vacuum)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
${\lambda}_{d}$ for electron $= \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mE}}$
$\lambda$ for photon $= \dfrac{hC}{E}$
Ratio $= \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mE}}\dfrac{E}{hC} = \dfrac{1}{C}\sqrt{\dfrac{E}{2m}}$

questions.q:
When UV light of wavelength $300 \mathrm{~nm}$ is incident on the metal surface having work function $2.13 \mathrm{eV}$, electron emission takes place. The stopping potential is:
(Given hc $=1240 \mathrm{eV} \mathrm{nm}$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\lambda}-\phi=\mathrm{e} . \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{s}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1240}{300} \mathrm{eV}-2.13 \mathrm{eV}=\mathrm{eVs} \\ & \Rightarrow 4.13 \mathrm{eV}-2.13 \mathrm{eV}=\mathrm{eVs} . \\ & \Rightarrow \text { So, } \quad \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{s}}=2 \mathrm{volt}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Proton $( P )$ and electron $( e )$ will have same de-Broglie wavelength when the ratio of their momentum is (assume, ${m}_{p} = 1849$~${m}_{e}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The De Broglie wavelength is& $\lambda = \dfrac{h}{mv}$

The momentum is given by~$p = mv$

The momentum of proton is~${p}_{p} = {m}_{p}{v}_{p}$

The momentum of electron is $p ' = {m}_{e}{v}_{e}$

Since~$h$~is the Planck's constant and it is given that both wavelengths are same, i.e.

${λ}_{p} = {λ}_{e}$,~so~${p}_{p} = p '$.

questions.q: In a photoelectric effect experiment a light of frequency $1 . 5$ times the threshold frequency is made to fall on the surface of photosensitive material. Now if the frequency is halved and intensity is doubled, the number of photo electrons emitted will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given, ${f}_{i} = {f}_{0}$. Now, $f = \dfrac{fi}{2} = \dfrac{f0}{2}$.

Since $\dfrac{f0}{2} < {f}_{0}$ i.e. the incident frequency is less than threshold frequency. Hence, there will be no emission of photoelectrons.

Therefore, current $= 0$ and no photo electrons will be emitted.

questions.q: A particle of mass $4M$ at rest disintegrates into two particles of mass $M$ and $3M$, respectively, having non zero velocities. The ratio of de-Broglie wavelength of particle of mass $M$ to that of mass $3M$ will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{p}$

Both the particles will move with momentum same in magnitude and opposite in direction.

So de Broglie wavelength of both will be same, i.e., ratio $1: 1$.

questions.q:
A $2mW$ laser operates at a wavelength of $500$ nm . The number of photons that will be emitted per second is:
[Given Planck's constant $h = 6.6 \times {10}^{- 34}Js,$ speed of light $c = 3.0 \times {10}^{8}m / s$ ]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$P = 2mW$
$\lambda = 500nm$
Number of photons will be emitted per second is,
$n = \dfrac{P}{\left(\dfrac{hc}{\lambda}\right)} = \dfrac{2 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 500 \times {10}^{- 9}}{6.6 \times {10}^{- 34} \times 3 \times {10}^{8}}$
$= 5 \times {10}^{15}$
